items.calibration: lower-melting elements such as Sn, Zn, Cd and Ag, but also higher melting as Au and Cu
items.crucible: closed tantalum crucibles with a flat bottom, situated on an alumina-disc
items.instrument: DTA 404 F1 Pegasus instrument from Netzsch
items.quote: Sample amounts of approximately 100-150 mg were used. Reference material was a comparable amount of NIST standard sapphire in a second tantalum crucible. The applied heating rate and inert gas flow was 5 K/min and 50 ml/min Ar, respectively. Depending on the range of measured temperatures, lower-melting elements such as Sn, Zn, Cd and Ag, but also higher melting as Au and Cu, were used for calibration.

items.calibration: six pieces of NIST-standard sapphire (30-50 mg each) as reference material
items.quote: Five pieces of a phase-pure sample (8-23 mg each) were dropped from ambient temperature into a bath of liquid tin (approximately 15 g) at 773 K. The enthalpy of solution was measured using a Tian-Calvet-type microcalorimeter (HT-1000 from Setaram [40]) as described in [41]. Aluminum oxide crucibles were used and calibration was performed using six pieces of NIST-standard sapphire (30-50 mg each) as reference material.

items.instrument: Bragg-Brentano diffractometer (Θ/2Θ-geometry), as well as a Guinier Camera
items.quote: Powder XRD was performed using a Bragg-Brentano diffractometer (Θ/2Θ-geometry), as well as a Guinier Camera.

items.quote: 17 samples with compositions between 4 and 60 at% Sn were prepared from 99.8 at% lithium wire (Alfa Aesar, Karlsruhe, Germany) and 99.95 at% tin ingot (Advent, Oxford, UK).
items.starting_materials: 99.8 at% lithium wire (Alfa Aesar, Karlsruhe, Germany) and 99.95 at% tin ingot (Advent, Oxford, UK)

items.label: Li81:5 Sn18:5
items.quote: The sample Li81:5 Sn18:5 , which was prepared a second time and showed the pure phase Li17 Sn4 (a1⁄4 19.7243(2)) without tin contaminations, was used for the measurements.
